lessons.title: Read features and trial conditions
lessons.description: Compare two fictional products while keeping specifications separate from an impression.
lessons.canDo: Read additive claims and degree without inventing test results

lessons.title: Choose for a purpose, with a stated condition
lessons.description: Follow negative comparisons, sufficient conditions and the limits of a review.
lessons.canDo: Identify the comparison direction and what remains untested

grammar.title: Add a second feature, without denying the first
grammar.formation: Plain V/i-adjective or noun + ばかりでなく/だけでなく; na-adjective + な + ばかりでなく/だけでなく. The added item often takes も.
grammar.explanation: Both patterns mean not only A but also B. A remains true. ばかりでなく often fits a more formal written review, while だけでなく is common in daily speech and writing; this tendency doesn’t make either universally wrong. Retrieve earlier だけ. This unit doesn’t require the stronger later ばかりか pattern.
grammar.example: この製品は軽いだけでなく、電池もいらない。
grammar.translation: This product is not only light; it also needs no battery.

examples.ja: この{製品|せいひん}は{軽|かる}いだけでなく、{電池|でんち}もいらない。
examples.en: This product is not only light; it also needs no battery.

examples.ja: {音|おと}が{静|しず}かなばかりでなく、{操作|そうさ}も{簡単|かんたん}だ。
examples.en: Not only is the sound quiet; operation is also simple.

examples.ja: {台本|だいほん}だけでなく、{配役|はいやく}も{読|よ}んだ。
examples.en: I read not only the script but also the cast list.

grammar.mistake: Keep な after a na-adjective, but don’t insert な after a noun. Do not choose between grammatical synonyms as if only one could mean addition.

grammar.title: Understand how great the degree is
grammar.formation: Plain V/i-adjective + ほど/くらい; na-adjective + な + ほど/くらい; noun + ほど/くらい. ぐらい is a variant of くらい.
grammar.explanation: A clause can illustrate the degree of the following description: 音が聞こえないほど expresses noise so strong that the sound cannot be heard. Degree ほど and くらい overlap in many positive contexts. Numerical approximation is not an exact measurement or an automatic maximum. This lesson separates a reviewer’s description from the stated measured weight.
grammar.example: 台詞が聞こえないほど、外の騒音が大きい。
grammar.translation: Outside noise is so loud that I cannot hear the line.

examples.ja: {台詞|せりふ}が{聞|き}こえないほど、{外|そと}の{騒音|そうおん}が{大|おお}きい。
examples.en: Outside noise is so loud that I cannot hear the line.

examples.ja: {装着|そうちゃく}していることを{忘|わす}れるくらい{軽|かる}く{感|かん}じた。
examples.en: It felt so light I almost forgot I was wearing it.

examples.ja: {台本|だいほん}を{読|よ}むのに、{十分|じゅっぷん}ほどかかった。
examples.en: Reading the script took about ten minutes.

grammar.mistake: ほど/くらい can both express degree; name the target in form practice. About ten minutes is approximate, not a promise that ten is the upper limit.

grammar.title: Keep the comparison direction in a negative sentence
grammar.formation: A は B ほど + adjective-negative. For example, A は B ほど重くない. Noun B precedes ほど without な.
grammar.explanation: A negative comparison says A doesn’t reach B’s degree on the stated scale. If B weighs 220 g and A 180 g, A is not as heavy as B. It doesn’t say A is heavier, or that every feature of A is better. A comparison with an expectation also reports a shortfall, not a measured universal fact.
grammar.translation: A is not as heavy as B.

examples.en: A is not as heavy as B.
B is not as cheap as A.

examples.ja: {雑音|ざつおん}は{思|おも}ったほど{少|すく}なくなかった。
examples.en: There was not as little noise as I had expected.

grammar.mistake: Track both objects and the adjective. 重くない is not 重い. Do not use the comparison alone to invent a specification.

grammar.title: Recognise an unexpected or minimal example
grammar.formation: Noun + (で)さえ; noun + に/で/と + さえ where that particle remains necessary. Taught action form: V-stem + さえする. Negative predicates can mean not even.
grammar.explanation: さえ highlights an extreme, surprising or minimal example in context. 説明書さえ読まなかった says even the manual was not read; it doesn’t say no reading of any kind ever happened. Preserve a location/recipient particle when its role is needed. An opinion using さえ is not a product specification.
grammar.example: 説明書さえ読まなかった。
grammar.translation: I didn’t even read the manual.

examples.ja: {説明書|せつめいしょ}さえ{読|よ}まなかった。
examples.en: I didn’t even read the manual.

examples.ja: {静|しず}かな{部屋|へや}でさえ{雑音|ざつおん}が{聞|き}こえた。
examples.en: Even in a quiet room, I could hear interference.

examples.ja: {台本|だいほん}の{人物|じんぶつ}の{名前|なまえ}さえ{分|わ}からなかった。
examples.en: I didn’t even know the names of the script’s characters.

grammar.mistake: さえ is not ordinary only だけ. Do not drop a required location で or read a negative example as a completed positive action.

grammar.title: Identify the one condition presented as enough
grammar.formation: Noun + さえ + Vば; noun + さえあれば; V-stem + さえすれば; Vて + さえいれば. Retrieve ば: ある→あれば, 読む→読めば, する→すれば.
grammar.explanation: The speaker presents one condition as sufficient for the stated result. ケーブルさえあれば、この有線の製品で聞ける is conditional on the cable being present and the already described compatible device. It doesn’t assert that the cable has arrived or that every device will work. This is as long as, not even if ても.
grammar.example: 付属品のケーブルさえあれば、この製品で聞ける。
grammar.translation: As long as I have the included cable, I can listen with this product.

examples.ja: {付属品|ふぞくひん}のケーブルさえあれば、この{製品|せいひん}で{聞|き}ける。
examples.en: As long as I have the included cable, I can listen with this product.

examples.ja: {説明書|せつめいしょ}を{確認|かくにん}しさえすれば、{設定|せってい}の{方法|ほうほう}が{分|わ}かる。
examples.en: If I just check the manual, I can find out how to configure it.

examples.ja: {音|おと}が{聞|き}こえてさえいれば、{合図|あいず}を{確|たし}かめられる。
examples.en: As long as I can hear the sound, I can check the cue.

grammar.mistake: Use the stem in 確認しさえすれば, not 確認するさえすれば. A condition doesn’t confirm that its result already happened.

dialogues.title: Try two fictional headphones before buying
dialogues.scene: After the script practice, Misaki and Bao compare two fictional headphones in a shop. A is wired, 180 g, 3,000 yen; B is wireless, 220 g, 5,000 yen. They try each for ten minutes in the same quiet room. The learner’s device has the compatible socket.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {台本|だいほん}の{朗読|ろうどく}を{聞|き}くなら、{製品|せいひん}の{性能|せいのう}だけでなく、{装着|そうちゃく}した{感|かん}じも{比|くら}べよう。
lines.romaji: Daihon no rōdoku o kiku nara, seihin no seinō dake de naku, sōchaku shita kanji mo kurabeyō.
lines.meaning: If we want to listen to the script reading, let’s compare not only performance but also how they feel when worn.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: Aは{有線|ゆうせん}で{百八十|ひゃくはちじゅう}グラム、{三千円|さんぜんえん}。Bは{無線|むせん}で{二百二十|にひゃくにじゅう}グラム、{五千円|ごせんえん}だね。
lines.romaji: A wa yūsen de hyakuhachijū guramu, sanzen-en. B wa musen de nihyakunijū guramu, gosen-en da ne.
lines.meaning: A is wired, 180 grams and 3,000 yen. B is wireless, 220 grams and 5,000 yen.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: Aは{軽量|けいりょう}で、{電池|でんち}の{交換|こうかん}もいらないね。Bの{良|よ}さも、{同|おな}じ{部屋|へや}で{試|ため}してから{考|かんが}えよう。
lines.romaji: A wa keiryō de, denchi no kōkan mo iranai ne. B no yosa mo, onaji heya de tameshite kara kangaeyō.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {静|しず}かな{部屋|へや}で{十分|じゅっぷん}ずつ{着|つ}けてみたよ。Aは{忘|わす}れるくらい{軽|かる}かった。
lines.romaji: Shizuka na heya de juppun zutsu tsukete mita yo. A wa wasureru kurai karukatta.
lines.meaning: I tried each for ten minutes in a quiet room. A was so light I almost forgot I was wearing it.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {前|まえ}の{視聴|しちょう}では、{早口|はやくち}の{語尾|ごび}を{聞|き}き{逃|のが}したね。{今回|こんかい}は{人物|じんぶつ}が{話|はな}す{場面|ばめん}を{同|おな}じ{音量|おんりょう}で{聞|き}こう。
lines.romaji: Mae no shichō de wa, hayakuchi no gobi o kikinogashita ne. Konkai wa jinbutsu ga hanasu bamen o onaji onryō de kikō.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: AでもBでも{合図|あいず}は{聞|き}こえた。でも、{外|そと}の{騒音|そうおん}が{大|おお}きい{場所|ばしょ}ではまだ{試|ため}していないよ。

lines.speaker: Misaki

lines.speaker: You

lines.meaning: Today I’ll just try them. Let’s decide later after considering where I listen to the script.

dialogues.title: A decision for home listening, with limits
dialogues.scene: That evening Bao and Misaki write a review at home. Prices include the accessories; no student discount or further price cut applies. Bao chooses A for the stated home use but has not bought it. B’s outside-noise feature remains untested.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {仕様|しよう}ではAは{百八十|ひゃくはちじゅう}グラムで、Bは{二百二十|にひゃくにじゅう}グラム。AはBほど{重|おも}くないね。
lines.romaji: Shiyō de wa A wa hyakuhachijū guramu de, B wa nihyakunijū guramu. A wa B hodo omokunai ne.
lines.meaning: The specifications say A is 180 grams and B 220. A is not as heavy as B.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {価格|かかく}は{付属品|ふぞくひん}を{含|ふく}めて{三千円|さんぜんえん}と{五千円|ごせんえん}。{値引|ねび}きも{学生|がくせい}の{割引|わりびき}もないから、BはAほど{安|やす}くない。
lines.romaji: Kakaku wa fuzokuhin o fukumete sanzen-en to gosen-en. Nebiki mo gakusei no waribiki mo nai kara, B wa A hodo yasukunai.
lines.meaning: Prices including accessories are 3,000 and 5,000 yen. There is no price reduction or student discount, so B is not as cheap as A.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {用途|ようと}は{家|いえ}で{台本|だいほん}の{朗読|ろうどく}を{聞|き}くことだね。Aの{長所|ちょうしょ}と{短所|たんしょ}を{両方|りょうほう}{書|か}こう。
lines.romaji: Yōto wa ie de daihon no rōdoku o kiku koto da ne. A no chōsho to tansho o ryōhō kakō.
lines.meaning: The intended use is listening to the script reading at home. Let’s write both A’s strengths and weaknesses.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: Aは{軽|かる}いばかりでなく、{電池|でんち}もいらない。{実用|じつよう}にはその{利点|りてん}があるけど、ケーブルは{移動|いどう}するときの{欠点|けってん}になる。
lines.romaji: A wa karui bakari de naku, denchi mo iranai. Jitsuyō ni wa sono riten ga aru kedo, kēburu wa idō suru toki no ketten ni naru.

lines.speaker: Misaki

if it’s; as for this case

grammar: ばかりでなく/だけでなく addition
watch.prompt: Optionally save a review claim from your own clip. Separate measured facts, impressions, test conditions and anything still unverified.

exercises.prompt: Which measured specification belongs to A?
exercises.explain: The second line gives A’s three figures; the lighter feeling is a separate impression.

exercises.prompt: What was held the same for both trials?
options: The room, ten-minute wearing time and listening volume
Loud outdoor noise and battery replacement
exercises.explain: They try each in the same quiet room for ten minutes at the same volume; they have not tested outdoors.

exercises.prompt: What do the stated terms allow after opening the package?
options: A return within a year automatically
A free extra cable after every listening session
No return under the stated shop terms
exercises.explain: A one-year warranty is stated separately from the no-return-after-opening condition.

exercises.context: Form practice: add a second feature with the named na-adjective pattern 静かなばかりでなく.
exercises.line: {音|おと}が{静|しず}か＿＿ばかりでなく、{操作|そうさ}も{簡単|かんたん}だ。
exercises.explain: 静か is a na-adjective and takes な before attributive ばかりでなく.

exercises.context: Form practice: add the cast list to the script with noun + だけでなく.
exercises.line: {台本|だいほん}＿＿、{配役|はいやく}も{読|よ}んだ。
exercises.explain: Nouns attach directly; the second reading is added, not a denial of the first.

exercises.context: Reply casually to Misaki. Respect the limits of a quiet-room trial.
exercises.line: {外|そと}の{騒音|そうおん}がある{場所|ばしょ}でも、{必|かなら}ず{聞|き}こえるかな。
options: {品質|ひんしつ}は{全員|ぜんいん}に{必|かなら}ず{同|おな}じだよ。
{外|そと}で{一時間|いちじかん}{試|ため}したから、{全部|ぜんぶ}{分|わ}かったよ。
その{場面|ばめん}ではまだ{試|ため}していないから、{今|いま}は{決|き}められないね。
exercises.explain: The first keeps the untested outside setting unknown; the other replies invent a universal claim or a trial.

exercises.meaning: In that scene, outside noise was so loud that I could not hear the ending. Use ほど.
tiles: {語尾|ごび}が{聞|き}こえないほど、
exercises.explain: The inability to hear illustrates the degree of noise. This model sentence is not an extra claim about the shop trial.

exercises.prompt: What decision has Bao made by the end?
options: Choose A for home listening, without buying yet
Buy B immediately with a student discount
exercises.explain: The last line chooses A for the stated purpose and says 購入はまだ.

exercises.prompt: What does AはBほど重くない mean with the stated weights?
options: A and B weigh the same

Whether Bao’s device has a cable socket
The effect of its outside-sound-reduction feature
exercises.explain: They state the feature exists, but its effect was not checked in this session.

exercises.context: Form practice: complete AはBほど重くない, using the negative i-adjective 重い.
exercises.explain: Drop the final い and use くない; A doesn’t reach B’s degree of heaviness.

exercises.context: Form practice: say even in a quiet room, retaining the location particle in 部屋でさえ.
exercises.line: {静|しず}かな{部屋|へや}＿＿{雑音|ざつおん}が{聞|き}こえた。
exercises.explain: で locates the hearing event; さえ adds the unexpected example. This is a model sentence, not the trial’s recorded result.

exercises.context: Form practice: use 確認します with the named stem + さえすれば pattern.
exercises.line: {説明書|せつめいしょ}を{確認|かくにん}＿＿さえすれば、{設定|せってい}の{方法|ほうほう}が{分|わ}かる。
exercises.explain: Remove ます to obtain 確認し before さえすれば. The claim presents that check as sufficient for finding the method.

exercises.context: Reply casually to Misaki. Confirm the stated condition and purpose, without claiming a purchase.
exercises.line: {家|いえ}で{朗読|ろうどく}を{聞|き}くなら、Aにする？
options: うん。その{用途|ようと}なら、{付属品|ふぞくひん}のケーブルさえあれば、{合図|あいず}も{聞|き}けるね。
うん。{昨日|きのう}もうBを{買|か}ったから、Aはいらない。
ケーブルは{必|かなら}ず{全|すべ}ての{端末|たんまつ}に{使|つか}えるよ。
exercises.explain: The first retains the compatible device and home purpose; the other replies invent a purchase or universal compatibility.

exercises.meaning: With my compatible device, as long as I have the included cable, I can hear the cue with this product.
tiles: {私|わたし}の{端末|たんまつ}なら、
{付属品|ふぞくひん}のケーブルさえあれば、
exercises.explain: The device context bounds the claim; さえあれば presents the cable as the sufficient condition.
